To determine $\mathrm{ex}_L(n, P_5)$ under the condition that $11 \mid n$, we analyze the maximum number of edges in a linear $3$-graph on $n$ vertices containing no linear path $P_5$.

A linear path $P_k$ in a $3$-uniform hypergraph has $k$ edges and $2k+1$ vertices. For $k=5$, $P_5$ has $2(5)+1 = 11$ vertices. Since $P_5$ is connected and contains 11 vertices, any linear $3$-graph whose connected components each have at most $11$ vertices and contain no $P_5$ will be $P_5$-free. 

The maximum number of edges in a linear $3$-graph on $v$ vertices is given by the maximum size of a partial Steiner triple system $D(2, 3, v)$ (the Schönheim bound). For $v = 11$:
$$D(2, 3, 11) = \left\lfloor \frac{11}{3} \left\lfloor \frac{10}{2} \right\rfloor \right\rfloor - 1 = \left\lfloor \frac{55}{3} \right\rfloor - 1 = 17.$$

An optimal linear $3$-graph on 11 vertices achieves this bound with 17 edges and contains no copy of $P_5$. Taking the disjoint union of $\frac{n}{11}$ copies of this 11-vertex extremal configuration yields:
$$\mathrm{ex}_L(n, P_5) = 17 \cdot \frac{n}{11} = \frac{17}{11}n.$$

ANSWER: \frac{17}{11}n
